reason: 'My son, give ear to my words.' The KJV singleton is real and the catalogue records it — at Alma 36:1, the opening of the blessing to Helaman, which Alma 38:1 deliberately repeats to the second son ('even as I said unto Helaman'). Adjudicating it twice would double-count a formula the chapter itself marks as a repetition. The corpus's other use is at 2 Nephi 9:40. See Alma 36:1.

sharedText: inasmuch as ye shall keep the commandments of God, ye shall prosper in the land
reason: The land covenant, quoted here in the same breath as the Psalm 5:1 exordium and flagged by the text itself as a repetition of what was said to Helaman at Alma 37:13. Its adjudication is at 1 Nephi 2:20, to 1 Kings 2:3. Worth one observation the register can hold: 38:1 reads 'ye shall be CAST off from his presence' where Alma 37:13, seventeen verses earlier, reads 'CUT off from his presence'. Neither wording is the KJV's — 1 Kings 9:7 has 'cut off' of Israel and the land, not of a presence — so the variation is internal drift in a formula the book has repeated for five hundred years of its own chronology, and it is evidence about the Book of Mormon rather than about its source.

'For blessed is he that endureth to the end.' 'Endureth to the end' is a KJV singleton at Matthew 10:22 and the machine ranks it first in the chapter, but the phrase has already been adjudicated in this book at Alma 32:13, where seven continuous words are reproduced ('he that findeth mercy and endureth to the end, the same shall be saved') and where the fusion with Matthew 24:13's apodosis is the finding. Alma 38:2 has three of those words and replaces the apodosis with a beatitude formula, which is the standing Book of Mormon form (2 Nephi 31:15-20, 3 Nephi 15:9). Alma reusing his own compressed version six chapters later is not a fresh borrowing (ADJUDICATING §4). See Alma 32:13.

sharedText: his voice was as thunder, and it shook the whole earth
reason: Alma's conversion is told three times in the Book of Mormon and twice by Alma himself in consecutive chapters. The biblical wording of the angelic voice is adjudicated at Alma 36:7, where the fuller telling supports links to both Acts 26:14 (the Damascus-road pattern) and Revelation 19:6 ('as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of mighty thunderings'). Alma 38:7 is the two-clause abridgement of that same sentence, delivered to a different son in the same week, and it introduces no biblical vocabulary the fuller telling lacks. See Alma 36:7.

The longest exact run the machine finds in this chapter — eight words — and it is the same run already adjudicated at Alma 36:10, in the parallel account, where the argument is that the Book of Mormon's third telling of the episode (Mosiah 27:23) lacks the nights and Alma's two first-person tellings supply them from Matthew's Jonah formula. Alma 38:8 is that second telling. The one thing it adds is 'the most bitter pain and anguish of soul', which is not Matthew's and whose nearest KJV neighbours ('anguish of spirit', Exodus 6:9; 'bitterness of soul', Job 7:11, 10:1) are too scattered to adjudicate. See Alma 36:10.

sharedText: he is the life and the light of the world
reason: 'Behold, he is the life and the light of the world.' The joining of light to life is adjudicated at Alma 28:14, where the catalogue notes that the KJV puts the two nouns together in one verse only. Alma 38:9 states the same title more fully, adding 'of the world' from John 8:12's 'I am the light of the world' and inverting John 1:4's order ('in him was life; and the life was the light of men') so that life comes first. The inversion is worth a reader's notice and is not enough to re-adjudicate. Note that the verse's other clause, 'no other way nor means whereby man can be saved', carries a link of its own at this verse to Acts 4:12. See Alma 28:14.

sharedText: receive you at the last day into his kingdom, to sit down in peace
reason: 'And may the Lord bless your soul, and receive you at the last day into his kingdom, to sit down in peace.' Sitting down in the kingdom is adjudicated at Alma 7:25, which reproduces two KJV singletons of Matthew 8:11 ('sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob', 'in the kingdom of heaven'). Alma 38:15 has the eschatological sitting without the patriarchs and without the KJV's phrase for the kingdom, and adds 'in peace', which is not Matthew's. Recorded so that a reader who arrives at the last verse of the farewell is sent to where the borrowing is argued. See Alma 7:25.
